recommendation: Keep this no-change audit. If FHIR-I still wants Age, Distance, or Count to become profiles in a future release, open a current issue that explicitly covers migration of all active datatype usages, extension value typing, serialization names, and generated artifacts.
issue_request: FHIR-16612 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It observed that Age, Distance, and Count were not used as Quantity-derived types and asked to make them STU immediately, then convert them to Quantity profiles during R5.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged implementation was git-svn commit 0b0fbffb3b3f1d2e53f541470345ab8b7b3fc89a, svn revision 14282, which changed source/fhir.ini so Age, Distance, and Count moved from normative to trial use. No later FHIR-16612-tagged source commit converted them to profiles.
additional_context: FHIR-9168 had previously made Quantity specializations real FHIR datatypes because they carry distinct semantics and serialize as their own choice-type names. Current source/fhir.ini still lists Age, Distance, and Count as active datatypes, not Quantity profile aliases, and the 2025 FHIR-I R6 maturity minutes explicitly list Age, Distance, and Count as normative. Current active StructureDefinition sources also use these datatype codes directly, including Condition.onset[x]/abatement[x], FamilyMemberHistory age fields, Device.count, Parameters.parameter.value[x], and Task input/output values. FHIR-50152 later cites Age, Count, and Distance in the R5/R6 Extension.value[x] allowed-type list.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit with no source change. Re-converting these datatypes to Quantity profiles now would be a broad normative/type-system change affecting active resource definitions and extension value typing, and would conflict with later R6 normative review evidence rather than safely completing a small missed application.
